component_opinions.item: Character identity and stable complete silhouette
component_opinions.evaluation: Roshan remains recognizable, but face/body contours drift and foreground duplication dominates the ending.

component_opinions.item: Exactly two connected mittens owned by Roshan
component_opinions.evaluation: A third oversized mitten enters at frame11; a fourth arrives later. Their sleeves connect to off-screen bodies, not Roshan.
The starting partial-fold grasp is readable, though its exact over/under contact is small at this input scale.

component_opinions.item: Existing mitten carries the attached flap
component_opinions.evaluation: Both authored mittens stay at the initial contact. The paper does not cross the remaining red crescent.

component_opinions.item: Same sweet supported on the same table
component_opinions.evaluation: The central sweet and gold sheet remain supported, but unsupported foreground arms obscure their evidence.

component_opinions.item: Gold paper occludes the remaining sweet surface
component_opinions.evaluation: The red crescent remains exposed throughout all41 canvases; no completed fold occurs.

component_opinions.item: Release leaves the useful fold intact
component_opinions.evaluation: Roshan never opens the original grip or leaves a closed fold. Extra arms are not a release.

component_opinions.item: Attention remains on useful task change
component_opinions.evaluation: Early gaze points toward the task, but later duplicated anatomy and body drift distract from any useful contact.

component_opinions.item: Golden paper and painted quilted material continuity
component_opinions.evaluation: Central gold and quilted material largely survive. Extra foreground mittens have a different oversized, muddier finish.
Rejected: no closure or release, plus catastrophic extra-hand ownership. It cannot contribute accepted pixels or motion to the actual wrapper.

qualification: All41 native896x512 canvases directly inspected on7 non-resampled boards plus three individual original-size details. A3 is reference-only and rejected. Source4.5 never transfers to action. Current in-game WRAP2.8 and the original full folding/neck/twist/release workflow remain open.
